issues.claim: Rule: equalities on the leading columns, then at most one range; no seek without a condition on the leading column.
issues.problem: The fetched excerpt of the design guide covers only included columns, so it does not show the column-order rule itself. The rule is standard SQL Server behaviour: no skip scan, and a range on the leading column leaves the next column to be checked only on the rows read. The explanation also derives it from the sort order, which the clustered/nonclustered excerpt supports ('rows are in sorted order', B-tree). The rebuttal's reference to the 'Column considerations' section is not backed by the excerpt, so keep the link title as it is and re-check that section when setting verified.
issues.suggestedFix: No change required. Optionally add a Learn page that shows a Seek Predicate with a residual Predicate (the showplan operators reference excerpt for Index Seek does this).
